title: U.S. Department of the Treasury Report: Homeowners Insurance Costs Rising, Availability Declining as Climate-Related Events Take Their Toll
organization: U.S. Department of the Treasury / Federal Insurance Office
claim_supported: Nationwide homeowners-insurance analysis covering more than 246 million policy-years; higher costs and reduced availability in higher-risk areas.
caveat: Data cover 2018-2022 and are aggregated to ZIP Code level; not a 2026 market snapshot.

title: Report on the Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 — Housing
claim_supported: Six percent of homeowners reported no homeowners insurance; affordability and lack of insurer availability were reported reasons.
caveat: Self-reported survey data; does not establish causation for any individual market.

title: Key Statistics & Data
claim_supported: As of June 2026 the FAIR Plan reported $768 billion of exposure and 696,562 dwelling and commercial policies in force.
caveat: Exposure is insured value, not probable catastrophe loss; FAIR Plan is an interested market participant.

title: Global natural catastrophe losses in 2025
claim_supported: Swiss Re estimated $107 billion of global insured natural-catastrophe losses in 2025, including about $40 billion from Los Angeles wildfires and more than $50 billion from severe convective storms.
caveat: Industry loss estimates can be revised; event attribution and insured-loss estimates are not forecasts of future years.

title: Sustainable Insurance Strategy
claim_supported: California links forward-looking catastrophe models and recognition of reinsurance costs to enforceable commitments to write more policies in wildfire-distressed areas.
caveat: California-specific regulatory structure; the Department is describing its own reform program.

title: 2026 Operating Budget
claim_supported: Citizens described major 2025 depopulation and projected a sharp reduction in policies in force as private-market capacity improved.
caveat: Citizens is an interested residual-market institution; projected counts can differ from realized counts.

title: High-Risk Series: National Flood Insurance Program
claim_supported: As of February 2025 FEMA owed Treasury $22.5 billion for NFIP even after $16 billion of debt cancellation in 2017; GAO calls for comprehensive reform.
caveat: GAO analysis concerns federal fiscal exposure, not a claim that every NFIP policy is underpriced.

title: Flood Insurance: FEMA's New Rate-Setting Methodology Improves Actuarial Soundness but Highlights Need for Broader Program Reform
claim_supported: Risk Rating 2.0 more closely aligns premiums with property-level flood risk while affordability and broader program design remain unresolved.
caveat: Predates later NFIP changes; use for design logic rather than current premium levels.

title: National Flood Insurance Program — community and floodplain management guidance
claim_supported: NFIP participation ties access to flood insurance to community floodplain-management responsibilities and mitigation requirements.
caveat: Program details can change; this guidance should not substitute for current local ordinances.

title: Terrorism Risk Insurance Program
claim_supported: TRIA created a shared public-private compensation framework for certified terrorism losses and is authorized through 2027.
caveat: Terrorism backstop design is not automatically transferable to cyber, pandemic, climate or AI.

title: TRIP Reports and Resources
claim_supported: Treasury continues to assess effectiveness and market participation under TRIP, including a June 2026 effectiveness report.
caveat: Program evidence concerns terrorism insurance; broader backstop analogies are the author's.

title: Pandemic Risk: Federal Insurance Approaches Would Entail Costs to Taxpayers and Businesses Might Not Participate
claim_supported: GAO found private insurance played a limited role in pandemic business losses and modeled federal approaches in which government would assume most or all of the risk.
caveat: Pandemic correlation differs from cyber, AI and natural catastrophe correlation.

title: Insurance Topics: Artificial Intelligence
claim_supported: NAIC documents state-regulatory work on insurer use of AI, including the 2023 Model Bulletin and third-party model oversight.
caveat: NAIC materials coordinate state regulation but are not themselves uniform binding law in every state.

title: NAIC Members Approve Model Bulletin on Use of AI by Insurers
claim_supported: The Model Bulletin sets governance, risk-management, testing and documentation expectations and reminds insurers that AI-supported decisions remain subject to existing insurance law.
caveat: A bulletin is not a model law or regulation and adoption varies by state.

title: Financial Stability Report — December 2025
organization: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
claim_supported: EIOPA identifies potential AI-related channels including common-model correlated behaviour, third-party dependencies, granular-segmentation demutualisation pressures and emerging AI-risk insurance markets.
caveat: European prudential analysis; scenarios and channels are not claims that systemic failure has already occurred.

title: Insurance Risk Dashboard
organization: European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority
claim_supported: July 2026 dashboard raised digitalisation and cyber risk to high, citing frontier AI, geopolitics and elevated cyber underwriting exposure.
caveat: Dashboard is an assessment framework, not a prediction of insured loss.

title: ILS market insights: February 2026
claim_supported: Swiss Re reported record 2025 ILS issuance of $24.7 billion and outstanding notional near $60 billion.
caveat: Issuer/intermediary market source; figures describe notional issuance, not expected catastrophe loss.

title: ILS market insights: July 2026
claim_supported: Catastrophe-bond issuance exceeded $17 billion across 64 transactions in the first half of 2026, the strongest first half on record according to Swiss Re.
caveat: Market data from an active participant; issuance volume does not by itself prove cheaper protection.

title: PBGC releases FY 2025 Annual Report
claim_supported: PBGC reported a fifth consecutive year in which both single-employer and multiemployer insurance programs had positive net financial positions.
caveat: Positive net position does not remove long-term policy, demographic or sponsor risks.

title: Private Health Insurance: Market Concentration Generally Increased from 2011 through 2022
claim_supported: GAO found three or fewer insurers held at least 80% of individual and employer-group market enrollment in at least 35 states.
caveat: Enrollment concentration is not by itself proof of anticompetitive conduct or the sole cause of premiums.

title: Insurance Topics: Long-Term Care Insurance
claim_supported: NAIC explains that older LTC blocks were often priced with immature experience; claim incidence/duration were understated and lapse rates lower than assumed, contributing to later rate increases.
caveat: General market history; individual policy blocks differ.

title: History — Coffee and Commerce
claim_supported: Lloyd's documents the late-seventeenth-century coffeehouse's role as a center of shipping information and marine underwriting and the later subscription market.
caveat: Lloyd's own institutional history; marine insurance predates Lloyd's and developed in multiple commercial centers.

title: FM History — From 1835 Innovation to Global Resilience Leadership
claim_supported: FM traces the Factory Mutual tradition to Zachariah Allen's loss-prevention approach and the use of engineering and inspections to reduce property loss.
caveat: FM's account of its own lineage; use for institutional history, not neutral comparative evidence.

title: Actuarial Standard of Practice No. 12: Risk Classification
claim_supported: ASOP 12 defines risk classification, adverse selection, credibility and the balance between homogeneity and practical/credible classes.
caveat: Professional guidance, not a social-policy rule about which classifications should be legal or fair.

title: Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program
claim_supported: World Bank describes sovereign disaster-risk finance as a way to increase post-disaster funding capacity without compromising fiscal balance and development objectives.
caveat: Program description and policy framework; outcomes depend on country design and implementation.

title: Protection Gaps in Insurance for Natural Hazards and Retirement Savings in Asia
claim_supported: OECD describes parametric coverage, faster payout potential and basis-risk tradeoffs in natural-hazard protection gaps.
caveat: Asia-focused report; examples do not imply identical market structure elsewhere.

title: The California Public Wildfire Model
claim_supported: California is developing a public wildfire catastrophe model intended to support insurance, mitigation, planning and public understanding of wildfire loss.
caveat: Model is under development in 2026; it is not yet a validated operational pricing model.

title: Reform made real — forward-looking wildfire catastrophe model review
claim_supported: California completed review of a forward-looking wildfire catastrophe model and tied model/reinsurance use to commitments to expand writing in distressed areas.
caveat: Department announcement describes intended regulatory effects; realized market outcomes require later evaluation.

title: Reports & Notices — Federal Insurance Office
claim_supported: Provides the underlying FIO homeowners-insurance analyses and other federal insurance research used for market context.
caveat: Index page; claims should be traced to the linked underlying reports where material.

title: Climate change presses on: Devastating wildfires and intense thunderstorms exacerbate losses for insurers
claim_supported: Munich Re reported that no hurricane struck the U.S. mainland in 2025 while wildfire, severe thunderstorms and floods still drove major losses; its insured-loss total was about $107 billion.
caveat: Industry loss estimates and peril classifications can differ from other catastrophe datasets; use as a second industry view rather than independent proof of attribution.

title: Lower losses, growing risks: the natural disaster review for the first half of 2026
claim_supported: Munich Re reported lower first-half 2026 natural-disaster losses than recent five-year averages while emphasizing that climate change and growing exposure continued to increase future loss risk.
caveat: Half-year figures are preliminary and a quiet period is not evidence of a lower long-run loss distribution.

title: Business Blackout
claim_supported: Lloyd's modeled a severe but plausible cyber attack on the U.S. power grid in which insurance claims arose across more than 30 lines, illustrating cross-line accumulation.
caveat: Scenario results are hypothetical stress-test outputs, not realized losses or forecasts; use only for accumulation logic.

title: Insuring AI: data centre value accumulation risks
claim_supported: Swiss Re describes AI data-centre projects with construction costs up to about $20 billion, dense physical and operational dependencies, and concentration across insureds and insurance lines.
caveat: Forward-looking sector analysis with limited loss history for next-generation facilities; project costs and capacity forecasts can change.

title: Natural catastrophes: the USD 424bn protection gap and adaptation to counter growing exposure
claim_supported: Swiss Re estimates a 2025 modeled natural-catastrophe protection gap of $424 billion and reports a median projected benefit-cost ratio of 1.86 across reviewed adaptation projects.
caveat: Protection-gap and benefit-cost figures are model- and project-set dependent; projected BCRs should not be treated as guaranteed realized returns.
